doc.title: Carmen Leggio interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998

title: Not listening to his own records and wrap-up
summary: At home he doesn't play his own music after losing loved ones; closing exchange.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: When you’re home by yourself and you’re listening, what do you like to listen to? What do you pick out?

Well I’ll tell you, again, I can never sit down and listen to my music in my house. My albums, I have the whole ten CD package of Maynard Ferguson, and I don’t put it on. I’ve lost a lot of people and I’m coming out of it now, but I’ve lost a lot of people, a lot of close ones in my life, so it’s to the point where unless I’m out playing, when I’m home I’m on the couch with the T.V., which is bad, it’s no good. So I should put my music on but I don’t do it. So really —
Well we’ll put it on here.
Well this has been a really fascinating time talking to you.
Oh same here, you’re very comfortable.
Is there anything that I haven’t asked you about that you think you’d like to talk about?
I don’t think so, no. I think we got it.
